source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

original_test_intent: Verify the four temperature records represented by `TEMP_GB_NVS1~4`—presumptively NVSwitch devices 1 through 4 on the GPU baseboard—are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct ASIC identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the platform specification.
original_method: Confirm GB and NVS terminology, resolve four stable BMC records, bind every NVS index to its physical GPU-baseboard ASIC, NVSwitch/fabric identity and BMC management source, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with per-device limits under recorded GPU/NVLink workload, fabric state and cooling. Preserve logs, fabric and hardware state.
manual_activity: The platform owner confirms GB/NVS semantics, identifies the four physical NVSwitch-class ASICs and their BMC/fabric mapping, and supplies per-device limits. Automation can collect four BMC records, fabric inventory and UI rows; a human resolves index/ASIC/source ambiguity and owns the verdict. No GPU/NVLink load, switch reset or baseboard service is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS and confirmation of the GB/NVS terminology
Per-index NVSwitch or other NVS ASIC physical location, vendor/device/part identity, firmware and stable UUID/fabric identifier where exposed
GPU/NVLink/NVSwitch topology and Fabric Manager inventory needed to correlate logical and physical identities
BMC management source for each temperature, including controller, bus, mux, device address and exact die/board field
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for each NVS1-4 sensor
Per-ASIC units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health and freshness specification
Recorded GPU/NVLink/fabric workload and power state, fan mode/speeds, baseboard airflow and any approved vendor telemetry equivalence
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel, NVIDIA XID or fabric logs; switch, NVLink, GPU and thermal history is relevant evidence.
Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_GB_NVS1~4'` unless that exact string is documented as one record. Enumerate and query NVS1 through NVS4 separately and preserve individual status.
Do not map NVS index to GPU slot or OS enumeration. Bind each record to a physical baseboard ASIC and stable fabric identity; neighboring GPU temperatures are separate sensors.

Treat I2C/I3C/management access as BMC/platform scope. Require controller/bus/mux/address and the exact field; `nvidia-smi`, Fabric Manager or NVSwitch tools alone do not prove the BMC target/value without approved equivalence.

Do not start GPU/NVLink traffic or stress, reset a switch or Fabric Manager, change fabric/link/power state, service the baseboard, alter fans/thresholds or flash firmware. Record the current passive state.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped ASICs, stale data or BMC/UI/fabric disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, GB/NVS definitions, baseboard/ASIC/fabric/BMC-bus topology, client and Script; build a four-device expectation matrix before collection.
Retrieve NVS1-NVS4 independently with complete SDR identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.

Correlate every BMC record with physical ASIC and stable NVSwitch/fabric identity plus recorded GPU/NVLink workload, power and cooling state; use vendor telemetry only if exact field equivalence is approved.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, GPU/fabric load, switch/FM reset, link/power/service, fan/threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Confirm GB/NVS semantics and approve the four-ASIC physical, fabric and BMC management-source map.
Provide per-ASIC thermal thresholds, tolerance, status, freshness and any NVSwitch/vendor telemetry equivalence, and approve the collection tool/Script.
Review NVS1 through NVS4 independently and issue the formal verdict without using GPU temperatures, a partial list or one ASIC as coverage for another.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove four NVS records. It omits baseboard ASIC/fabric/bus/UI/spec mapping, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate complete sensors, confirm four GPU-baseboard NVS ASIC identities and BMC telemetry sources, resolve every vendor-supported record and query it through protected read-only access, then correlate four UI rows with the physical/fabric matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_GB_NVS1~4, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or exercising GPU/NVSwitch fabric.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a four-row matrix keyed by GPU-baseboard NVS ASIC and stable BMC sensor, documenting physical location, part/firmware, fabric identity/topology and management bus/source, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with per-device limits under a recorded passive fabric/cooling state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact GPU-baseboard/NVSwitch/fabric population and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/GPU-baseboard, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, NVSwitch firmware/Fabric Manager/driver, GPU/NVLink topology, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: GPU-baseboard schematic/layout and NVS index map, NVSwitch/fabric inventory, BMC management-bus/sensor definition, ASIC thermal limits, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves a range into four physical NVSwitch-class ASIC-bound records and adds fabric/management-source evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static NVS temperatures do not validate NVLink/NVSwitch traffic, fabric functionality, bandwidth, links, XID/fabric errors, throttling, reset, firmware or alarm/protection behavior; GPU temperatures are separate coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: GB/NVS ASIC/fabric/bus map, per-device acceptance, workload/cooling timing rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: NVS numbering can differ among schematic, BMC and fabric tools; readings may be die or board sensors; UI polling can lag and different baseboard variants can change ASIC population.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or NVIDIA/NVSwitch telemetry as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/field and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate NVS1-4 identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. GPU die temperature or aggregate fabric health is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS, confirmed GB/NVS terminology and four-row NVS ASIC physical location, part/firmware and stable fabric-identity matrix
GPU/NVLink/NVSwitch topology and Fabric Manager inventory used only for identity correlation
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source for each NVS1-4 record
Complete separate raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps plus separate redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Per-ASIC Project/vendor specification and recorded GPU/NVLink/fabric load/power plus fan/baseboard airflow state with tolerance/update-lag and any approved telemetry comparison

Explicit missing/duplicate/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-load/no-reset/no-service/no-retry proof, final GPU/fabric/BMC health and engineer-owned four-ASIC verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The range is unsuitable as a literal query and GB/NVS needs Project confirmation, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive display/specification validation of four temperature records. The exact ASIC/fabric/source mapping is a readiness input, not a conflicting test purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The four-record passive thermal purpose is identifiable and plausibly targets GPU-baseboard NVSwitch devices. Project SPEC can confirm terminology, topology and acceptance, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification while refining generic GPU/board-zone language to presumptive GPU-baseboard NVSwitch ASICs and requiring stable fabric plus BMC-bus identity.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, GPU-slot temperature or aggregate fabric evidence from being presented as four NVS ASIC temperatures, and prevents GPU/NVLink stress or switch resets from being added to a passive display test.
independent_technical_reasoning: On a GPU baseboard, NVS commonly denotes NVSwitch devices rather than GPU slots or generic thermal zones. Each BMC index therefore needs a physical ASIC, stable fabric identity and management-source mapping. NVIDIA tooling can corroborate the ASIC only after its temperature field is shown equivalent; passive BMC display validation provides no authority for load, reset or fabric testing.
